newsitem.title: NORWAY: Hydro helps push up Norwegian share index.
newsitem.headline: Hydro helps push up Norwegian share index.

text.p: Norwegian shares rose following gains by industrial giant Norsk Hydro, pharmaceutical group Nycomed and offshore service company Petroleum Geo-Services on Tuesday.
But both engineering and offshore group Aker and investment group Resource Group International RGI fell in bourse trade after a surprise announcement they planned to merge.
The Total index was up 0.71 percent at 845.80 points in healthy volume of 731 million crowns.
Hydro, which has a weighting of about 20 percent on the Total index, rose 1.48 percent to 309 crowns in what appeared to be a partial correction after Monday's losses, dealers said.
Hydro came under selling pressure on Monday following company comments on the outlook for second-half profits.
Nycomed A shares ended 6.45 percent higher at 82.50 crowns following market rumours it would be taken over by a major European drug company, traders said. Nycomed declined comment.
Petroleum Geo-Services finished 5.75 percent higher at 184 crowns after announcing it had issued four million American Depositary shares (ADS) at $27.25 per share.
Aker A shares dropped 0.8 percent to 131.50 crowns while RGI fell 7.6 percent to 61 crowns.
